```{r, eval = TRUE, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
if (!ml_ready) {
  cat("> This copy of the guide was built without a training environment, so the",
      "code is shown without its output. See `vignette(\"models\")` to set one up.\n")

```

This walkthrough trains the tiny square transformer on CPU within the
package's smoke limits: at most 512 positions, 20 optimiser steps, 600 seconds
and two threads. It shows every stage working: data from the rules engine,
training, a checkpoint, an exact resume, and a legal move by the trained model.
It does not produce a strong opponent, and no result here should be read as
one.

```{r}
env <- Sys.getenv("G3_ML_ENV")
work <- file.path(tempdir(), "g3-training")
options(gambitR3D.ml_env = env, gambitR3D.registry_dir = file.path(work, "registry"))
gambitR3D::g3_setup_ml(env)$status
```

## Data

Training data comes only from the rules engine: positions from short games
labelled by the alpha-beta teacher, tactical fixture games played to a real
result, and positions where a platform carries a single piece, so that
platform actions are not missing from the data. Every record stores its state,
its complete legal-action list, its targets and its split; whole games are
assigned to splits.

```{r}
dataset <- list(seed = 20261026L, games = 8L, positions = 160L, max_walk_plies = 24L,
                platform_positions = 16L, teacher = list(nodes = 2000L, depth = 3L))
```

## Train, stop, resume

```{r}
cfg <- list(profile = "tiny", seed = 20261026L, steps = 12L, batch_size = 32L, threads = 2L,
            chunk_steps = 4L, evaluate = "validation")
part1 <- gambitR3D::g3_train_model(c(cfg, list(max_steps_this_run = 6L, register = FALSE)),
                                   dataset, file.path(work, "run"))
part1$status
part2 <- gambitR3D::g3_train_model(c(cfg, list(resume_from = part1$checkpoint$path)),
                                   dataset, file.path(work, "run"))
rbind(part1$metrics, part2$metrics)[, c("step", "loss", "policy_loss", "grad_norm", "top1_agreement")]
part2$model[c("parameter_count", "weights_changed")]
```

Loss values need not fall steadily in a dozen steps, and they need not here.
What the run checks is that every loss and gradient is finite, the weights
change, and the resumed run continues exactly where the first one stopped.
The win/draw/loss head learns only from games that reached a real result;
positions from games cut off at a ply limit carry no outcome target.

## Play with the checkpoint

```{r}
model <- part2$model_id
st <- gambitR3D::g3_new_game()$state
d <- gambitR3D::g3_choose_action(st, agent = paste0("model:", model),
                                 budget = list(mode = "mcts", simulations = 16L))
d$label
d$action_id %in% gambitR3D::g3_legal_actions(st)$action_id
```

The model scores only actions the engine says are legal, and the engine checks
the chosen action again before applying it.

## Self-play

```{r}
sp <- gambitR3D::g3_self_play(list(model = model, games = 2L, max_plies = 40L, simulations = 8L,
                                   seed = 1L), file.path(work, "self-play"))
sp$games[, c("game_id", "plies", "status", "result", "termination")]
```

A game stopped at the ply cap is recorded as `truncated`, never as a draw.

## Running it in the background

In the app (Training, "Train opponent") or from R, the same run can be a
background job with progress, cancellation and resume:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
job <- gambitR3D::g3_start_job(list(
  type = "training",
  args = list(config = c(cfg, list(ml_env = env)), dataset = dataset, output_dir = file.path(work, "job")),
  limits = list(wall_seconds = 600)
))
gambitR3D::g3_job_status(job)$progress
gambitR3D::g3_cancel_job(job)
job2 <- gambitR3D::g3_resume_job(job)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
gambitR3D:::.g3_ml_shutdown()
```
